correctness.rationale: The three Bell-pair-times-product pure states are each separable across one cut. Their equal mixture has normalized rational density matrix with exact partial-transpose spectra [1/3±sqrt(2)/6, ±sqrt(2)/6, 0,0,1/6,1/6] across each of three one-qubit cuts; the negative eigenvalue -sqrt(2)/6 excludes cut-separability. For finite-dimensional continuous nonnegative faithful pure-cut seeds, each separate convex roof attains its minimum and is zero exactly on the cut-separable set. Thus all three factors in mixed R2 are positive while each pure component has R2=0. This proves strict nonconvexity and positive value on a biseparable mixture; no exact positive R2 numerical value or LOCC counterexample is claimed.

value.rationale: The counterexample separates a cutwise-entangled mixed state from genuinely multipartite entanglement defined by the convex hull of biseparable pure states. It exposes a concrete structural defect of the order convex-roof-each-partition-then-geometric-mean in a published quantity, and motivates using a single full convex roof rather than mistaking fixed-cut inseparability for genuine multipartite entanglement.
